caption: A pot of jam boils on a stove, and the surface foams up and bubbles thickly.

sa.check: The pot is on a stove.
The boil comes first and the foaming follows.

pc.expect: The foam only rises while the pot stays on the heat and sinks back only when it is pulled off.
pc.fail: The foam sinks back while the pot sits on the burner with nothing changed; or the foam rises and falls in turn on the heat; or the foam stays up after the pot has been pulled off and left standing; or the foam rises before any bubble appears.

pc.expect: The jam is a thick liquid whose bubbles push up slowly, hold their domes for a moment and burst heavily, leaving the surface mounded.
pc.fail: The jam bubbles as thin and fast as water; or the surface holds a fixed shape while bubbles burst through it; or the jam sets solid in the pot; or the foam stands as rigid spikes that keep their shape when the pot is moved.

pc.expect: The bubbles rise from below to the surface and burst there, and the jam stays in the pot unless it climbs over the rim.
pc.fail: Bubbles sink from the surface toward the pot's floor; or hang still in the jam; or the jam climbs the pot's outside and goes in over the rim; or jam lifts off the surface and hangs above it.

pc.expect: Foam high in the pot means the jam below has risen: the level and the foam go up together.
pc.fail: The foam reaches the rim while the jam below is calm and far from full; or the jam's level drops while the foam climbs; or the foam climbs while the surface below shows no bubbles at all.

pc.expect: One pot of jam; the jam stays in the pot except where it spills over the rim.
pc.fail: Jam passes through the pot's wall; or the level jumps up with nothing added; or a second pot appears; or the pot changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pot, the hob and the jam's colour stay the same.
pc.fail: The pot changes colour; or the jam changes colour; or the hob's knobs move by themselves.
